I fixed what was on my list for the Works set (W1, W2 and W3), redrew seven plates (all except W4), remade the state pictures and the behind picture, exported again, checked every view and drew the sheets. I paid for nothing and committed nothing. The lead made snapshot commits while I worked. The notice corner is unchanged: its stills match round 4's byte for byte, and nothing under pit-village changed.

**What I changed**

- **People at work in both lit doorways (finding 1).** I used the existing figure shapes, all dressed in one near-black cloth and kept out of the yards' strong lights, so they show as dark shapes against the lit back wall.
  - No. 2: one man stoops over the lathe, seen from behind; one stands side-on at the press with his hand raised. Both are in every No. 2 plate; only the lathe man stays in W2 slowed.
  - No. 1: one weaver stoops at a loom, seen from behind; one stands side-on with a hand on a loom. They appear only in the "men gone" and working plates, so on "go" the men leave the gate and appear inside.
  - The masks now take in the doorway. They cover about 12% of the frame for "men gone", 14% for W2 slowed, 8% for the behind picture and 74% for working.
  - To stop a crate stack hiding the press man from W2, No. 2's gateway now has three crates instead of four.
- **The waiting men are a loose crowd (finding 2).**
  - At No. 1: two rows in front of the shut gate, backs to the camera, 0.5 to 1 m between the middles of their bodies, sizes varied by 0.96 to 1.04 so the heads sit at different heights.
  - The stooped man is at the brazier, which now stands against the gate's right leaf.
  - A thin rim of light falls on the men: a cool light from the yard and a warm one from the lamp's side, and they reach nothing else. The lantern does not light their backs.
  - No. 2's eight men stand the same way for page 12.
  - I made No. 1's shut cart doors a paler weathered timber, so the men's heads and the gate bars show dark against them.
  - In W3 at film size you can count the heads (sheet below). At a 360-pixel-wide phone copy they are small but separate.
- **The drums (findings 2 and 7, film helper's problem 6).** I could not put PETROL and DIESEL against the dividing wall right of No. 1's right pier. From W1's new spot, 3 m nearer, everything right of that pier lies past 0.93 across, so they would be cut off and past the phone-button line.
  - Instead they stand in front of the crowd's left end (No. 2's: the right end). Nobody stands between them and W1, W2 or W3.
  - The words are whole in every view: 0 to 3% hidden. They stay in must_read.
  - "DIESE" in W3 is fixed.
- **Pop-up crates (finding 7).** They stand two side by side with one on top, in the middle of the gateway. From W1's composed spot all three THIS WAY UP show whole (4% of the crate group hidden; the limit is 5%). I wrote a new check file, works-w1-working-shot-check.json, with the crates in must_read.
- **Cameras 3 m nearer (finding 3).** W1 and W2 now go from 10.0 m to 8.8 m from the works wall (y 12.0 to 13.2); the slide is still 1.2 m. The nearest man stands 7.4 m from the composed spot, and the gate fills about half the frame's width. DIESEL reaches 0.72 down.
- **New checker test (rule 7).** A check file can now set "story_reaches_down" (the lowest point a story thing must reach). It is off unless a file sets it. I set 0.70 in the W1, W1 working, W2 and W2 slowed files, and all pass at 0.72.
- **W1 light (finding 5).**
  - The gate lamp now hangs from the outer pier's inner face, over the gateway, at 7 W (half of round 4's 14 W). It lights only the gate, chain, board, men and yard. Its light sits 0.2 m toward the lane from the glass, so the board catches it.
  - The fire is 80 W (was 110) and no longer lights the piers. No. 1's yard light went from 260 W to 900 W, so the bars stand dark against the pale doors.
  - W2 is mirrored.
- **No. 1's looms (finding 6).** They are now chest-high, with upright side frames, a big spoked driving wheel belted up to a small shaft hung from the ceiling, and a pale roll of cloth.
  - Both back walls are broken up with a darker lower part and shelves of boxes and tins.
  - No. 1 has a bobbin rack; No. 2 has a workbench with a vice and a rack of metal bars.
- **Handcart (finding 12, first half).** It carries three THIS WAY UP crates facing W3. It sits at the right pavement's kerb; in W3 its middle is 0.86 across and its wheels reach 0.80 down.
- **The stooped man (finding 13).** I traced round 4's measurements. One of the checker's five downward rays started inside the brazier's rim, 0.22 m from its middle, because his outstretched arms made his outline box reach over it. It was not his feet, so the warning was false. I wrote this in the W1 and W3 check files. He now stands on the ground, overlapping the brazier by 41 pixels.

The new set arrived at 04:42, so there was no need to give up waiting. Nothing was paid for and I committed nothing. The notice corner draws exactly as before: its two stills are the same file, byte for byte.

**Smoke (finding 4)**
- **Wind:** it now blows across the view, toward No. 1's side, a little away and sinking slightly. Each plume lies on its side as a trail.
- **Look:** the smoke is a brownish grey, measured at about 95 on screen in W3. For their first 2 seconds the puffs are small and close together, so the plume stays attached to the chimney's mouth.
- **I traced the paths before drawing**, with my own tracer (smoke_trace.py), which reads the new cameras from works-shot.json.
  - In W3, No. 2's plumes run left at about 0.24 to 0.28 down, below the lower rule card, which ends at 0.236. They fade out at about 0.45 across. That is just before No. 1's chimney at 0.375; a longer plume ran on behind it and looked like No. 1's smoke.
  - In W1 and W2 the trails run left along the top of the frame, under the words.
- **The rings:**
  - **Not the focus blur:** I drew the same frame with and without the blur, and the rings were identical.
  - **The cause:** with the wind blowing straight away from the cameras, the puffs stacked one behind another. Their shades differed a lot (0.72 to 1.14), so each puff's outline showed as a ring. Drawing the puffs all one shade and unrotated made the rings vanish.
  - **The fix:** the cross wind, and shades kept close (0.93 to 1.07). I also made the puff picture white all over, so its soft edge can't fade toward black.

**Labels in W3 (finding 8)**
- `callout()` has a new option, `wordsWithLine`, so the words come in with the line. It also has an optional corner in the line and a fixed side for the words. Left out, the label draws exactly as before: 10 of 10 stills of the old chapter 2, including its existing labels, are identical.

- **Jumps:** the only ones are the planned ones.
  - The cut to W1 on "In" is one step of 40.7 (the frames either side change about 0.4).
  - The time cut on "go" is one step.
  - The three window steps on "start" are 13.6, 8.4 and 6.8.
  - The cut to W3 on "Most" is one step of 50.2.
  - Both page turns start gently.
  - The run-on from page 4 into page 5 changes 0.6 at most, and no place where two chunks meet jumps.
- **Camera:** the audit finds 0 problems. The aim never turns (0.0000 degrees) and the lens stays at 60.4. Both slides are 1.2 m, now from 12.0 to 13.2 m up the lane.
- **Words:** all 29 typed lines are short forms of what Malina says on that page. Each comes in 0.09 to 0.15 s after its spoken word. No line goes past 0.884 across, and no digits are typed.
- **Fixed since round 4, as seen in the film:**
  - the men stand as a crowd you can count;
  - workers show inside both lit doorways;
  - all three THIS WAY UP crates in W1 show whole words;
  - the NEW MONEY SPENT arrow ends at the chain;
  - MACHINES is readable for 0.83 s and points at the flywheel;
  - BANK is dim;
  - the smoke has no rings.

**Problems, worst first**
1. **PRICES arrow strikes through "No. 2" (105.96 to 107.15 s, page 5).** Its tip runs straight across the "No. 2" board, right at the page's conclusion, PRICES UP. It reads as the name crossed out. The cameras now stand 3 m nearer, so the board is bigger, and the arrow is still drawn at fixed pixels.
2. **The level PRICES arrow crowds the "No. 1" board (73.1 to 74.3 s, page 3).** The word PRICES touches the board's left edge and the arrow runs along the board's bottom edge. Same cause.
3. **The frame is still not full top to bottom.**

6. **The waiting men are flat, pure-black cut-outs.** No rim light shows even with the picture brightened 2.5 times, and the middle three merge into one shape.
7. **"busy" reads as the lights dipping, not as busier.** The windows go 26 levels darker at 79.4 s and the doorway turns grey at 80.2 s (40 levels darker). Nothing brightens. The press man turns reddish during the burst.

The checkout (view C1, the film's opening picture) is built, composed and tested in the film stage. At the composed spot, the shot checker finds no problems in 29 checks. Nothing was paid for: Poly Haven is free (CC0) and the fonts are free (OFL).

**What I built** (scripts in film-kit/paper-film/blender/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/checkout/, results in film-kit/assets/models/inflation-chapter-2-newcomers/checkout/):
- **The room:** one checkout lane in a small New Zealand supermarket at closing time, built by script from an empty scene.
  - A dark open ceiling. The rows of lights near the queue are off, which leaves the top band dark for the typed words.
  - The shop window, blue-black. Through it, small and dim, a petrol station's canopy lettered PETROL · DIESEL. It has no brand, and its price board is turned edge-on.
  - The ends of two aisles. A lane on each side of ours.
  - The till, and the operator's empty stool.
  - A hanging CHECKOUT sign with no number.
- **The story group, touching:** a full grey wire basket on the belt, with the divider bar against its front.
  - In the basket: a paper bag printed BREAD, a milk bottle labelled MILK, BUTTER, CHEESE, apples, kiwifruit, a lemon, avocados, and bananas over the rim.
  - Beyond the basket: the newspaper bill in its wire stand, reading NEW MONEY: / PRICES WILL / GO UP in 0.1 m poster letters.
  - The card terminal stands on the ledge just right of the bill. Its keypad is turned away and has no digits on it anyway.
- **Lettering:** every word is real and its own sharp surface in the film. There are no digits, prices, brands or chain colours anywhere. Everything is neutral greys and wood.
- **The newspaper's name:** THE EVENING LAMP. I searched for:
  - "Evening Lamp" newspaper New Zealand: no such paper.
  - "The Evening Lamp" New Zealand business: none found.
  - "Evening Lamp" NZ: only lamp shops.

checkoutCritique.summary:
I compared the checkout view C1 against the notice corner (its film frames and its plate and painting), plan 34 part 1 section B, and pages 1, 15 and 16. I looked at the plate at full and phone size, the Blender composed render, the stage stills and both checker reports. I also drew five more stage stills across the slide (1.5, 2.4, 3.4, 4.4 and 5.4 s), and measured brightness, colour and how much of the frame the story group covers.

**Builder's claims that hold up:**
- The belt's lines meet at 0.50 across, 0.50 down, on the bill's left edge.
- The camera is level and never turns (the same rotation at both spots).
- The story group runs 0.426 to 0.776 down (the basket 0.595 to 0.752).
- The bill is 2.71 times as bright as the frame's average.
- Every word shows whole, and there are no digits, brands or chain colours.
- The bill's words are a short form of the narration ("If new money is created... prices will go up").
- No tearing in any of my five extra stills.
- The notice corner is untouched: its stills at 4.5 s and 10 s have the same checksums as round 4's (90fb30e8… and 35b68c22…), and git shows no change under pit-village.
- The biggest repository file is 23 MB, and none of the new files is a .blend.

**The masthead:** I searched "The Evening Lamp" and "Evening Lamp" on the open web. I also checked all 1,617 New Zealand newspaper titles listed on nznewspapers.org, which is built from the National Library's open data.
- No paper has that name.
- Titles with "Lantern" exist (Lantern, New Zealand Lantern), as do many "Evening ___" titles, so do not rename it to Lantern.
- "The Lamp" is a US Catholic magazine, not an NZ paper.
- Papers Past blocked my automatic search, so I could not check it.
- The name passes.

**The judgement:** the frame does not reach the notice corner's standard yet.
- At phone size it reads as a small lit display in a black void. The top 40% of the frame is nearly black.
- The bottom fifth is an empty tan belt that is brighter than the story.
- The story group is about half the size of the notice corner's.
- Several props read as models or toys.
- A newcomer gets "checkout" and "prices will go up" in 2 seconds. "Full basket" is weaker (it is mostly apples). "Supermarket" is at risk: a large lit PETROL · DIESEL sign over shelves of plain boxes can read as a petrol station shop.

**Two things the builder got wrong:**
- The slide's-start frame's worst checker problem is not "the dark belt". It is the spare-divider tray (two triangular bars in a U-shaped tray) in the bottom-left corner. The check file does not name it, so the checker called it a shadow.
- That slide's-start frame is also the chapter's last held image (about 10 s at the end of page 16), and it still fails 3 checks.

**What I could not judge:** how the Flux painting will change any of this. I paid for nothing and changed no project files. My working files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Music/02fc5154-76f5-5aac-a505-860164e7e921/scratchpad/redesign/check-round-5-checkout (regions.py, phone-compare.jpg, crops, stage/ stills, slide-basket-row.jpg).

It is large and bright: the fascia spans about 0.37 of the frame's width at 0.41 down, its letters are 22 px tall, its brightness reaches 0.64 at the 95th percentile (the third brightest thing), and white pumps rise behind the shelves. There is no reflection or sill to say it is outside the glass, so it reads as a sign inside the shop. Together with CHECKOUT and grey steel shelves of plain boxes (they look like storage racks, not aisle ends), a newcomer can read 'a petrol station shop' rather than 'a supermarket'. It also sits exactly where page 1's label THE WARNING will go, left of the bill at 0.4 to 0.55 down, so two pieces of lettering would compete.
findings.fix:
Make the outside read as outside:
- Push the canopy to about y 60 and drop 'canopy-light' to about 100, so the fascia letters are about 12 to 14 px and dim.
- Add glass cues: a faint (5 to 8%) reflection of the lit interior on the window, and a visible sill.

Give the quiet side one plain supermarket cue: replace one steel shelf unit with a low produce display (bins or crates of apples, kiwifruit and bananas, using the Poly Haven models already downloaded, with no lettering), dimmer than the basket.

findings.where: Top band (title area) and the lit tube: ceiling-structure beam at y = 0 lit by 'bounce-to-ceiling' and 'ceiling-fill'; ceiling-light-16 (x -1.8, y 6.4), tube glow 3.5
findings.problem: In the composed frame the nearest ceiling beam's underside is a grey slab of brightness 0.27 to 0.33. That is above the frame's average of 0.21, and it sits across the title area (0.06 to 0.12 down, 0 to 0.47 across), where INFLATION and the other top-band words are typed. White type would straddle its hard lower edge. The checker's 'titles in dim sky' test passed only because it averages the whole band (0.06). Also, the lit tube at the left (0.03 to 0.24 across, 0.30 down) reaches 0.93 on the stage still and 0.96 in Blender, brighter than the bill's 0.89. It is a bright horizontal streak on the quiet side that points at nothing.
findings.fix: Keep the bounce and fill lights off the ceiling beams (light linking, as already done for the bill), or move the beam rows so none sits between y -1.1 and y 1.0. Then the title area measures under 0.10 at every point, not just on average. Lower the visible tube's glow so its peak stays under the bill's, about 0.8 (glow about 1.5), or switch off that fitting. Then the bill holds the brightest pixels as well as the brightest area.
